questions.question_text:
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.37 & 0.94 & 1.68 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.6443 & 0.8264 & 0.9535 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find $P(z < 0.94)$.

options.why: Complemented the table value, which gives the area to the right of $0.94$ instead of the left.
Subtracted $0.5$, which gives only the area between $0$ and $0.94$.
Read the $z = 1.68$ column of the table instead of the $z = 0.94$ column.

questions.question_text:
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 1.13 & 1.31 & 2.42 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.8708 & 0.9049 & 0.9922 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find $P(z > 1.31)$.

options.why: Read $P(z<1.31)$ straight off the table without taking the complement.
Used the $z = 1.13$ column, giving $1 - 0.8708$ instead of $1 - 0.9049$.
Subtracted $0.5$ instead of $1$ when taking the complement.

questions.question_text:
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.71 & 1.24 & 1.96 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7611 & 0.8925 & 0.9750 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find $P(0.71 < z < 1.96)$.

options.why: Used the $z = 1.24$ column as the upper boundary instead of $z = 1.96$.
Added the two table values instead of subtracting them, giving a probability greater than $1$.
Gave $1 - 0.9750$, the tail above $1.96$, instead of the strip between the two $z$-scores.

questions.question_text:
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.58 & 1.09 & 2.13 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7190 & 0.8621 & 0.9834 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find $P(z < -1.09)$.

options.why: Read $P(z<1.09)$ and ignored the negative sign on the $z$-score.
Subtracted $0.5$ from the table value instead of using symmetry and the complement.
Used the $z = 0.58$ column, giving $1 - 0.7190$ instead of $1 - 0.8621$.

questions.question_text:
The masses of a breed of dog are normally distributed with a mean of $24.0$ kg and a standard deviation of $3.5$ kg.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.60 & 0.86 & 1.00 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7257 & 0.8051 & 0.8413 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that a randomly chosen dog has a mass greater than $26.1$ kg.

options.why: Read $P(z<0.6)$ off the table without taking the complement for 'greater than'.
Subtracted $0.5$ from the table value instead of subtracting it from $1$.
Used the $z = 0.86$ column, giving $1 - 0.8051$ instead of $1 - 0.7257$.

questions.question_text:
A sample of $600$ eggs has masses that are normally distributed with a mean of $58.0$ g and a standard deviation of $4.0$ g. Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 1.28 & 1.60 & 2.05 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.8997 & 0.9452 & 0.9798 \\ \hline\end{array}$
How many eggs are expected to have a mass less than $51.6$ g?

options.why: Truncated $32.88$ instead of rounding it to the nearest whole egg.
Used $P(z<1.60) = 0.9452$, which is the proportion heavier than $51.6$ g.
Read the $z = 1.28$ column instead of the $z = 1.60$ column.

questions.question_text:
The times taken to complete a puzzle are normally distributed with a mean of $95$ seconds and a standard deviation of $20$ seconds.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.83 & 0.84 & 0.85 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7967 & 0.7995 & 0.8023 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Using the table, find the approximate time below which the fastest $20\%$ of times fall.

options.why: Used $z = +0.84$ instead of $z = -0.84$, giving the slowest $20\%$ boundary.
Chose $z = 0.83$, whose table value $0.7967$ is further from $0.8000$ than $0.7995$ is.
Gave the distance $z\sigma$ below the mean rather than the time itself.

questions.question_text:
The annual rainfall in a region is normally distributed with a mean of $640$ mm and a standard deviation of $110$ mm.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.50 & 1.00 & 1.50 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.6915 & 0.8413 & 0.9332 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that a year's rainfall is between $585$ mm and $750$ mm.

options.why: Subtracted the table values directly, forgetting that $P(z<-0.5)$ is $1 - 0.6915$, not $0.6915$.
Gave only $P(z<-0.5)$, the tail below $585$ mm.
Gave the complement of the correct area, which is the rainfall outside the interval.

questions.question_text:
The masses $M$ of adult men can be modelled by the Normal distribution with mean $80\text{ kg}$ and standard deviation $4\text{ kg}$.
Following standardisation, which of the following would give you the correct answer to $P(M>78)$?

options.why: Uses the lower tail at the standardised boundary instead of the upper tail.
Standardises 78 using the wrong distance from the mean.
Uses the wrong positive standardised value for a mass of 78 kilograms.

questions.solution_text: Standardise 78: $z=(78-80)/4=-0.5$. Thus $P(M>78)=P(Z>-0.5)$. By symmetry of the standard Normal distribution, this equals $P(Z<0.5)$, written here as $P(Z\le0.5)$.

options.why: Uses an inaccurate standard-normal table value for $z=1$.
A standard normal variable has substantial probability below $1$.
This is the upper-tail probability $P(Z>1)$, not the lower tail.
